source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא הָעָ֔ם כִּֽי־בֹשֵׁ֥שׁ מֹשֶׁ֖ה לָרֶ֣דֶת מִן־הָהָ֑ר וַיִּקָּהֵ֨ל הָעָ֜ם עַֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ אֵלָיו֙ ק֣וּם׀עֲשֵׂה־לָ֣נוּ אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר יֵֽלְכוּ֙ לְפָנֵ֔ינוּ כִּי־זֶ֣ה׀מֹשֶׁ֣ה הָאִ֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הֶֽעֱלָ֨נוּ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם לֹ֥א יָדַ֖עְנוּ מֶה־הָ֥יָה לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw the people that delayed Moses to come down from the mountain, and assembled the people against Aaron and said to him, arise, make for us gods who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from [the] land of Egypt, not we know what has happened to him.

en.L: And the people saw that Moses delayed to come down from the mountain, and the people gathered around Aaron and said to him, "Arise, make for us gods who will go before us, for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him."
en.B: The people saw that Moses was a long time in coming down from the mountain. So they crowded around Aaron and said to him, "Get up and make us gods to lead the way for us. This Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we have no idea what has become of him."
en.R: Moses stayed on the mountain a long time. When the people saw that he was not coming down, they crowded around Aaron. They said, "Come on, make us gods to lead us. We do not know what has happened to Moses, the man who led us out of Egypt."

es.L: Y vio el pueblo que Moisés tardaba en bajar del monte, y el pueblo se reunió en torno a Aarón y le dijeron: «Levántate, haznos dioses que vayan delante de nosotros, porque a este Moisés, el hombre que nos hizo subir de la tierra de Egipto, no sabemos qué le ha pasado».
es.B: El pueblo vio que Moisés tardaba mucho en bajar del monte. Entonces se agolparon alrededor de Aarón y le dijeron: «Anda, haznos dioses que nos abran camino. Ese Moisés, el hombre que nos sacó de la tierra de Egipto, no tenemos idea de lo que ha sido de él».
es.R: Moisés se quedó mucho tiempo en el monte. Cuando el pueblo vio que no bajaba, rodearon a Aarón y le dijeron: «Vamos, haznos dioses que nos guíen. No sabemos qué le ha pasado a Moisés, el hombre que nos sacó de Egipto».

fr.L: Et le peuple vit que Moïse tardait à descendre de la montagne, et le peuple s’assembla autour d’Aaron, et ils lui dirent : « Lève-toi, fais-nous des dieux qui iront devant nous, car ce Moïse, l’homme qui nous a fait monter du pays d’Égypte, nous ne savons pas ce qui lui est arrivé. »
fr.B: Le peuple vit que Moïse tardait à redescendre de la montagne. Ils se pressèrent alors autour d’Aaron et lui dirent : « Allons, fais-nous des dieux qui marchent devant nous. Car ce Moïse, l’homme qui nous a fait monter du pays d’Égypte, nous n’avons aucune idée de ce qu’il est devenu. »
fr.R: Moïse est resté longtemps sur la montagne. Quand le peuple a vu qu’il ne redescendait pas, tous se sont rassemblés autour d’Aaron. Ils lui ont dit : « Allez, fabrique-nous des dieux pour nous guider. Nous ne savons pas ce qui est arrivé à Moïse, l’homme qui nous a fait sortir d’Égypte. »

sw.L: Na watu wakaona kwamba Musa alichelewa kushuka kutoka mlimani, na watu wakakusanyika kumzunguka Haruni, wakamwambia, "Simama, utufanyie miungu itakayokwenda mbele yetu, kwa maana huyu Musa, mtu aliyetupandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri, hatujui kilichomtokea."
sw.B: Watu walipoona kwamba Musa amekaa muda mrefu bila kushuka kutoka mlimani, walimsonga Haruni pande zote, wakamwambia, "Amka, utufanyie miungu ya kutuongoza njiani. Huyu Musa, mtu aliyetupandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri, hatujui amekuwaje."
sw.R: Musa alikaa mlimani kwa muda mrefu. Watu walipoona kwamba hashuki, walimzunguka Haruni. Wakasema, "Haya, tutengenezee miungu ya kutuongoza. Hatujui kilichompata Musa, yule mtu aliyetutoa Misri."

vi.L: Dân chúng thấy Môi-se chậm xuống núi, thì dân chúng tụ tập quanh A-rôn và nói với ông: "Hãy đứng dậy, làm cho chúng tôi các thần để đi trước chúng tôi, vì Môi-se này, người đã đem chúng tôi lên khỏi xứ Ai Cập, chúng tôi không biết điều gì đã xảy đến cho ông ta."
vi.B: Dân chúng thấy Môi-se ở trên núi lâu quá mà chưa xuống, nên họ kéo đến vây quanh A-rôn và nói với ông: "Hãy đứng lên làm cho chúng tôi các thần để dẫn đường cho chúng tôi. Còn Môi-se này, người đã đưa chúng tôi lên khỏi xứ Ai Cập, chúng tôi không biết ông ta ra sao rồi."
vi.R: Môi-se ở trên núi rất lâu. Khi dân chúng thấy ông chưa xuống, họ kéo đến vây quanh A-rôn. Họ nói: "Nào, hãy làm cho chúng tôi các thần để dẫn dắt chúng tôi. Chúng tôi không biết chuyện gì đã xảy ra cho Môi-se, là người đã dẫn chúng tôi ra khỏi Ai Cập."

ko.L: 그리고 백성은 모세가 산에서 내려오는 것이 늦어지는 것을 보았다. 그러자 백성이 아론에게 몰려와서 그에게 말했다. "일어나서 우리 앞에서 갈 신들을 우리에게 만들어 주십시오. 우리를 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 올린 그 사람, 이 모세로 말하자면, 그에게 무슨 일이 일어났는지 우리가 알지 못합니다."
ko.B: 백성은 모세가 산에서 오랫동안 내려오지 않는 것을 보고, 아론에게 몰려가서 말했다. "자, 우리를 앞장서서 이끌어 줄 신들을 만들어 주십시오. 우리를 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 낸 그 사람, 모세라는 자는 어떻게 되었는지 도무지 알 수가 없습니다."
ko.R: 모세는 산 위에서 오랫동안 내려오지 않았다. 백성은 모세가 내려오지 않는 것을 보고 아론에게 몰려가서 말했다. "어서 우리를 이끌어 줄 신들을 만들어 주십시오. 우리를 이집트에서 데리고 나온 모세라는 사람이 어떻게 되었는지 모르겠습니다."

decisions.choice: gods: plural, since the verb with it is plural
alternatives: make us a god who will go before us
decisions.reason: The word can mean the one God or many gods. When it means Israel's God it takes singular verbs; here the verb "will go" is plural, so the people ask for gods. Yet Aaron makes a single calf and proclaims a feast to Yahweh (verses 4-5), so they may have meant an image standing for Israel's own God. Nehemiah 9:18 retells the story with the singular, "This is your god"; Acts 7:40 quotes the request as "Make us gods".

decisions.choice: delayed: was long in coming
decisions.reason: Moses had gone up into the cloud on the mountain and stayed there forty days and forty nights (24:18). To the people below, he seemed lost.

decisions.choice: this Moses, the man: spoken with scorn
decisions.reason: "This Moses" sets him at a distance. The people credit Moses, not God, with bringing them out of Egypt, and now they want something else to go before them, in place of the God who went before them in the pillar of cloud (13:21).

decisions.choice: Get up / Come on ... to lead the way
decisions.reason: "Arise" urges Aaron to act at once; Balanced and Readable use everyday words for it. "Go before us" means to lead, as the pillar of cloud did; Literal keeps "go before".

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("vit", "s'assembla", "dirent"); passé composé at Readable ("a vu", "ont dit"); speech keeps the tenses of speech
decisions.reason: As the French style guide sets: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative, the passé composé that of the plain Readable level.

decisions.choice: "miungu ya kutuongoza njiani" / "ya kutuongoza" (gods to lead us)
alternatives: "miungu itakayokwenda mbele yetu" at every level
decisions.reason: "To go before" someone means to lead them, as the pillar of cloud did (13:21); Balanced and Readable say "lead", as the English does, while Literal keeps "go before us".

decisions.choice: The people speak to Aaron in 합쇼체 ("만들어 주십시오", "알지 못합니다")
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet: the people speak to Moses and Aaron in 합쇼체. Their scorn is carried by the words "이 모세로 말하자면" and "모세라는 자" (meaning decision m3), not by dropping the polite ending.

decisions.choice: "신들", plural
decisions.reason: The verb with the word is plural (meaning decision m1), so Korean keeps the plural "신들" at every level.

decisions.choice: The people say "chúng tôi" and call Aaron "ông"; they speak of Moses as "ông ta"
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch terms note sets for the people speaking to Moses and Aaron. "ông ta" carries the scorn of "this Moses" (meaning decision) without an insult.

decisions.choice: "các thần" (plural)
decisions.reason: The plural follows the Hebrew verb (meaning decision); Vietnamese marks it with "các".

source.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲלֵהֶם֙ אַהֲרֹ֔ן פָּֽרְקוּ֙ נִזְמֵ֣י הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁר֙ בְּאָזְנֵ֣י נְשֵׁיכֶ֔ם בְּנֵיכֶ֖ם וּבְנֹתֵיכֶ֑ם וְהָבִ֖יאוּ אֵלָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to them Aaron, tear off [the] rings of the gold which [are] in [the] ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters, and bring [them] to me.

en.L: And Aaron said to them, "Tear off the rings of gold that [are] in the ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters, and bring [them] to me."
en.B: Aaron told them, "Pull the gold rings out of the ears of your wives and your sons and daughters, and bring them here to me."
en.R: Aaron answered, "Get the gold earrings from your wives, your sons and your daughters. Bring them to me."

es.L: Y Aarón les dijo: «{{plural_you:Arranquen|Arrancad}} los anillos de oro que [están] en las orejas de {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} mujeres, de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos y de {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} hijas, y {{plural_you:tráiganmelos|traédmelos}}».
es.B: Aarón les respondió: «{{plural_you:Quítenles|Quitadles}} los aretes de oro a {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} mujeres y a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos e hijas, y {{plural_you:tráiganmelos|traédmelos}} aquí».
es.R: Aarón les contestó: «{{plural_you:Pídanles|Pedidles}} los aretes de oro a {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} esposas, a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hijos y a {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} hijas. {{plural_you:Tráiganmelos|Traédmelos}}».

fr.L: Et Aaron leur dit : « Arrachez les anneaux d’or qui [sont] aux oreilles de vos femmes, de vos fils et de vos filles, et apportez-[les]-moi. »
fr.B: Aaron leur répondit : « Ôtez les anneaux d’or des oreilles de vos femmes, de vos fils et de vos filles, et apportez-les-moi. »
fr.R: Aaron leur a répondu : « Prenez les boucles d’oreilles en or de vos femmes, de vos fils et de vos filles. Apportez-les-moi. »

sw.L: Na Haruni akawaambia, "Ng'oeni pete za dhahabu zilizo masikioni mwa wake zenu, na wana wenu, na binti zenu, mniletee [hizo]."
sw.B: Haruni akawaambia, "Ondoeni pete za dhahabu masikioni mwa wake zenu, na wa wana wenu na binti zenu, mziletee hapa kwangu."
sw.R: Haruni akawajibu, "Chukueni hereni za dhahabu za wake zenu, za wana wenu na za binti zenu. Mniletee."

vi.L: A-rôn nói với họ: "Hãy tháo những khuyên vàng ở tai vợ các ngươi, con trai các ngươi và con gái các ngươi, rồi đem [chúng] đến cho ta."
vi.B: A-rôn bảo họ: "Hãy gỡ những khuyên vàng trên tai vợ, con trai và con gái của anh em, rồi đem đến đây cho tôi."
vi.R: A-rôn trả lời: "Hãy lấy những bông tai bằng vàng của vợ, con trai và con gái anh em, rồi đem đến cho tôi."

ko.L: 그러자 아론이 그들에게 말했다. "너희 아내와 너희 아들과 너희 딸의 귀에 있는 금고리를 빼서 나에게 가져오너라."
ko.B: 아론이 그들에게 말했다. "너희 아내와 아들딸들의 귀에 걸린 금귀고리를 빼서 나에게 가져오너라."
ko.R: 아론이 대답했다. "너희 아내와 아들과 딸에게서 금귀고리를 받아서 나에게 가져오너라."

decisions.choice: the rings of gold: likely jewelry asked from the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Israel left Egypt with articles of silver and gold given by the Egyptians (3:22; 11:2; 12:35-36). The gold God gave his people on the way out is now gathered for an idol. Later the people give their jewelry freely for the tabernacle (35:22).

decisions.choice: tear off: remove with force
decisions.reason: The verb means to tear away or strip off. The same verb is used in verse 3 and verse 24.

decisions.choice: Aaron speaks to the people in 해라체 with 너희 ("가져오너라")
decisions.reason: Aaron is the leader left in charge (24:14) and gives the people orders; Korean gives him the plain style a leader uses to a crowd, as Moses speaks to the people at Literal and Balanced in the term sheet.

decisions.choice: Aaron says "các ngươi" and "ta" (Literal); "anh em" and "tôi" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Aaron speaks to the people as Moses does in the Pentateuch terms note: "anh em" and "tôi" at Balanced and Readable, the plural "các ngươi" at Literal.

source.text: וַיִּתְפָּֽרְקוּ֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם אֶת־נִזְמֵ֥י הַזָּהָ֖ב אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּאָזְנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּבִ֖יאוּ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And tore off from themselves all the people the rings of the gold which [were] in their ears, and they brought [them] to Aaron.

en.L: And all the people tore off the rings of gold that [were] in their ears and brought [them] to Aaron.
en.B: So all the people stripped the gold rings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.
en.R: Everyone pulled off their gold earrings and handed them over to Aaron.

es.L: Y todo el pueblo se arrancó los anillos de oro que [estaban] en sus orejas, y [los] trajeron a Aarón.
es.B: Así que todo el pueblo se quitó los aretes de oro de las orejas y se los llevaron a Aarón.
es.R: Todos se quitaron sus aretes de oro y se los entregaron a Aarón.

fr.L: Et tout le peuple arracha les anneaux d’or qui [étaient] à leurs oreilles, et ils [les] apportèrent à Aaron.
fr.B: Tout le peuple se dépouilla donc des anneaux d’or qu’ils avaient aux oreilles, et ils les apportèrent à Aaron.
fr.R: Tout le monde a enlevé ses boucles d’oreilles en or, et les a données à Aaron.

sw.L: Na watu wote wakajing'olea pete za dhahabu zilizokuwa masikioni mwao, wakamletea Haruni [hizo].
sw.B: Basi watu wote wakajivua pete za dhahabu masikioni mwao, wakamletea Haruni.
sw.R: Kila mtu alivua hereni zake za dhahabu, akampa Haruni.

vi.L: Cả dân chúng tháo những khuyên vàng ở tai mình và đem [chúng] đến cho A-rôn.
vi.B: Vậy cả dân chúng gỡ những khuyên vàng trên tai mình và đem đến cho A-rôn.
vi.R: Mọi người đều tháo bông tai vàng của mình ra và đem nộp cho A-rôn.

ko.L: 그리고 모든 백성이 자기 귀에 있는 금고리를 빼서 아론에게 가져왔다.
ko.B: 그러자 온 백성이 자기 귀에서 금귀고리를 빼서 아론에게 가져왔다.
ko.R: 모든 사람이 금귀고리를 빼서 아론에게 갖다주었다.

decisions.choice: all the people tore off from themselves: every one of them took part, at once
decisions.reason: The verb form means they stripped the rings off themselves. "All the people" stresses that the whole people joined in, as readily as they had once said, "All that Yahweh has spoken we will do" (24:3).

source.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח מִיָּדָ֗ם וַיָּ֤צַר אֹתוֹ֙ בַּחֶ֔רֶט וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֖הוּ עֵ֣גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he took [it] from their hand and he fashioned it with the tool and he made it a calf of cast metal. And they said, these [are] your gods, Israel, who brought you up from [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And he took [it] from their hand and fashioned it with an engraving tool and made it a calf of cast metal. And they said, "These [are] your gods, O Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt."
en.B: He took the gold from them, shaped it with an engraving tool, and made it into a calf of cast metal. Then they said, "Israel, these are your gods, who brought you up from the land of Egypt!"
en.R: Aaron took the gold from them and shaped it with a tool. He made it into a statue of a young bull out of melted metal. Then the people said, "Israel, here are your gods who brought you out of Egypt!"

es.L: Y él [lo] tomó de su mano y le dio forma con un buril, y lo hizo un becerro de metal fundido. Y dijeron: «Estos [son] tus dioses, Israel, que te hicieron subir de la tierra de Egipto».
es.B: Él recibió el oro de sus manos, le dio forma con un buril y lo convirtió en un becerro de metal fundido. Entonces ellos dijeron: «¡Israel, estos son tus dioses, los que te sacaron de la tierra de Egipto!».
es.R: Aarón recibió el oro y le dio forma con una herramienta. Con el metal fundido hizo la estatua de un toro joven. Entonces el pueblo dijo: «¡Israel, aquí están tus dioses, los que te sacaron de Egipto!».

fr.L: Et il [le] prit de leur main, et il le façonna avec un burin, et il en fit un veau de métal fondu. Et ils dirent : « Voici tes dieux, Israël, qui t’ont fait monter du pays d’Égypte. »
fr.B: Il reçut l’or de leurs mains, le façonna au burin et en fit un veau de métal fondu. Alors ils dirent : « Israël, voici tes dieux, qui t’ont fait monter du pays d’Égypte ! »
fr.R: Aaron a pris l’or qu’ils lui donnaient, et il l’a travaillé avec un outil. Avec le métal fondu, il a fabriqué la statue d’un jeune taureau. Alors le peuple a dit : « Israël, voici tes dieux qui t’ont fait sortir d’Égypte ! »

sw.L: Naye akapokea [hiyo] mkononi mwao, akaitengeneza kwa kifaa cha kuchongea, akaifanya kuwa ndama wa chuma kilichoyeyushwa. Nao wakasema, "Hawa [ndio] miungu yako, Israeli, waliokupandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri."
sw.B: Akaipokea dhahabu kutoka kwao, akaiunda kwa kifaa cha kuchongea, akaifanya kuwa ndama wa chuma kilichoyeyushwa. Kisha wakasema, "Ee Israeli, hawa ndio miungu yako waliokupandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri!"
sw.R: Haruni alichukua dhahabu ile, akaiunda kwa kifaa. Akatengeneza sanamu ya fahali mchanga kwa chuma kilichoyeyushwa. Ndipo watu wakasema, "Ee Israeli, tazama miungu yako iliyokutoa Misri!"

vi.L: Ông lấy [vàng] từ tay họ, dùng dụng cụ khắc mà tạo hình nó, và làm nó thành một con bò con [bằng kim loại] đúc. Rồi họ nói: "Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, đây [là] các thần của ngươi, là các thần đã đem ngươi lên khỏi xứ Ai Cập."
vi.B: Ông nhận vàng từ tay họ, dùng dụng cụ khắc tạo hình, rồi làm thành một con bò con bằng kim loại đúc. Bấy giờ họ nói: "Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, đây là các thần của ngươi, là các thần đã đem ngươi lên khỏi xứ Ai Cập!"
vi.R: A-rôn nhận vàng từ tay họ và dùng dụng cụ để tạo hình. Ông làm ra một tượng bò con bằng kim loại nấu chảy. Rồi dân chúng nói: "Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, đây là các thần của ngươi, là các thần đã đem ngươi ra khỏi Ai Cập!"

ko.L: 그리고 그가 그들의 손에서 [그것을] 받아, 새기는 도구로 그것을 다듬어 부어 만든 송아지로 만들었다. 그러자 그들이 말했다. "이스라엘아, 이것들이 너를 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 올린 너의 신들이다."
ko.B: 아론은 그들에게서 금을 받아 새기는 도구로 모양을 다듬어, 금속을 부어 만든 송아지를 만들었다. 그러자 그들이 외쳤다. "이스라엘아, 이것이 너를 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 올린 너의 신들이다!"
ko.R: 아론은 그들에게서 금을 받아 도구로 모양을 냈다. 그는 녹인 금속을 부어 송아지 상을 만들었다. 그러자 사람들이 외쳤다. "이스라엘아, 이것이 너를 이집트에서 데리고 나온 너의 신들이다!"

decisions.choice: fashioned it with an engraving tool: the exact process is uncertain
alternatives: tied it up in a bag
decisions.reason: The word for the tool is used elsewhere only of a stylus for writing (Isaiah 8:1). It may mean Aaron shaped or finished the gold with a carving tool. Some take the verb and noun differently: that he formed it in a mold, or that he tied the gold up in a bag (a similar word means "bags" in 2 Kings 5:23). The result is clear either way: a calf of cast metal.

decisions.choice: a calf of cast metal: an image of a young bull
decisions.reason: The word means a young bull, a picture of strength. Images of bulls were used in the religions of Egypt and Canaan, and a god could be shown standing on one. The metal was melted and poured, so this is a cast image, which God's law had just forbidden (20:4, 23; 34:17).

decisions.choice: these are your gods: plural, though there is one calf
alternatives: This is your god, O Israel, who brought you up
decisions.reason: Both the word and the verb "brought you up" are plural, as in verse 1. Jeroboam later says the same words over his two golden calves (1 Kings 12:28). Nehemiah 9:18 retells this verse with the singular, "This is your god who brought you up from Egypt".

decisions.choice: a statue of a young bull out of melted metal
decisions.reason: Readable says what a "calf of cast metal" is: an image of a young bull, made from melted metal. It says "calf" from then on.

decisions.choice: "un becerro de metal fundido" (L, B); "la estatua de un toro joven" (R), then "el becerro", here and through chapters 32-34
decisions.reason: "Becerro" is the usual Spanish for a young bull in this story; "ternero" is the farm word and sounds too small and tame. "De metal fundido" says plainly how it was made.

decisions.choice: "un veau de métal fondu" (L, B); "la statue d'un jeune taureau" (R), then "le veau", here and through chapters 32-34
decisions.reason: "Veau" is the word for a young bovine, as the Hebrew is; "de métal fondu" keeps "cast metal" plain. "Le veau d'or" is the familiar name of the story, but the text itself does not say "golden calf", so it is not used in the translation.

decisions.choice: "ndama wa chuma kilichoyeyushwa" (L, B); "sanamu ya fahali mchanga" (R), then "ndama", here and through chapters 32-34
decisions.reason: "Ndama" is a young bovine, as the Hebrew word is. "Chuma kilichoyeyushwa" (melted metal) describes the casting in everyday words; "chuma" here is metal in general, not iron.

decisions.choice: "부어 만든 송아지" (L, B); "송아지 상" (R)
alternatives: "젊은 황소 상" at R, as the English Readable
decisions.reason: The image is of a young bull (meaning decision m2). Korean "송아지" is the familiar name of this image and still names a young animal of the herd; Readable adds "상" so that it is plainly a statue. The plural "신들" stays, though there is one calf (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: "con bò con bằng kim loại đúc" (Literal, Balanced); "tượng bò con" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The words of the Vietnamese Psalm 106:19 and 1 Kings 12:28 for the calf; Readable says it is a statue, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַיַּ֣רְא אַהֲרֹ֔ן וַיִּ֥בֶן מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לְפָנָ֑יו וַיִּקְרָ֤א אַֽהֲרֹן֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר חַ֥ג לַיהוָ֖ה מָחָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And saw Aaron and he built an altar before it, and called Aaron and said, a feast to Yahweh [is] tomorrow.

en.L: And Aaron saw [it], and he built an altar before it. And Aaron called out and said, "A feast to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} tomorrow!"
en.B: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf and made a proclamation: "Tomorrow we hold a feast to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}."
en.R: When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of the calf. Then he announced, "Tomorrow we will have a feast to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}!"

es.L: Y [lo] vio Aarón, y edificó un altar delante de él. Y Aarón proclamó y dijo: «¡Fiesta {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} mañana!».
es.B: Al ver esto, Aarón construyó un altar delante del becerro e hizo este anuncio: «Mañana celebraremos una fiesta {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}».
es.R: Cuando Aarón vio esto, construyó un altar delante del becerro. Luego anunció: «¡Mañana haremos una fiesta en honor {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}!».

fr.L: Et Aaron [le] vit, et il bâtit un autel devant lui. Et Aaron proclama et dit : « Fête pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} demain ! »
fr.B: Voyant cela, Aaron bâtit un autel devant le veau et fit cette proclamation : « Demain, il y aura une fête pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. »
fr.R: Quand Aaron a vu cela, il a construit un autel devant le veau. Puis il a annoncé : « Demain, nous ferons une fête en l’honneur {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ! »

sw.L: Naye Haruni akaona [hayo], akajenga madhabahu mbele yake. Naye Haruni akatangaza, akasema, "Kesho ni sikukuu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!"
sw.B: Haruni alipoona hayo, akajenga madhabahu mbele ya ndama, akatangaza, "Kesho tutafanya sikukuu kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}."
sw.R: Haruni alipoona hayo, alijenga madhabahu mbele ya ndama. Kisha akatangaza, "Kesho tutakuwa na sikukuu ya kumheshimu {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}!"

vi.L: A-rôn thấy [vậy], thì xây một bàn thờ trước nó. A-rôn kêu lên và nói: "Ngày mai [là] một kỳ lễ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}!"
vi.B: Thấy vậy, A-rôn xây một bàn thờ trước tượng bò con và tuyên bố: "Ngày mai chúng ta sẽ giữ lễ cho {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}."
vi.R: Thấy vậy, A-rôn xây một bàn thờ trước tượng bò con. Rồi ông loan báo: "Ngày mai chúng ta sẽ mở tiệc để tôn vinh {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}!"

ko.L: 그리고 아론이 [그것을] 보고 그 앞에 제단을 쌓았다. 그리고 아론이 외쳐 말했다. "내일은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 드리는 절기다!"
ko.B: 아론은 이것을 보고 송아지 앞에 제단을 쌓은 다음, 이렇게 공포했다. "내일 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 절기를 지키겠다."
ko.R: 아론은 이것을 보고 송아지 앞에 제단을 쌓았다. 그리고 큰 소리로 알렸다. "내일 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 높이는 잔치를 열겠다!"

decisions.choice: Aaron saw: what he saw is not stated
alternatives: Aaron was afraid (the same consonants can be read as "he feared")
decisions.reason: He saw the calf, or saw how the people received it (verse 4). Either way, his next steps lend the calf the forms of true worship.

decisions.choice: a feast to Yahweh: the calf is honored under the name of Israel's God
decisions.reason: Aaron does not proclaim a feast to a foreign god but to Yahweh. The sin is not only turning to other gods but making an image to stand for the true God, which the second of the Ten Words forbids (20:4-5).

decisions.choice: in front of the calf
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "before it"; Balanced and Readable name the calf.

source.text: וַיַּשְׁכִּ֨ימוּ֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיַּעֲל֣וּ עֹלֹ֔ת וַיַּגִּ֖שׁוּ שְׁלָמִ֑ים וַיֵּ֤שֶׁב הָעָם֙ לֶֽאֱכֹ֣ל וְשָׁת֔וֹ וַיָּקֻ֖מוּ לְצַחֵֽק׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And they rose early on [the] next day and offered up burnt offerings and brought near peace offerings. And sat the people to eat and to drink, and they rose up to play.

en.L: And they rose early on the next day and offered up burnt offerings and brought near peace offerings. And the people sat down to eat and to drink, and they rose up to play.
en.B: They were up early the next morning, offering burnt offerings and bringing fellowship offerings. Then the people sat down to a meal of food and drink, and rose up to revel.
en.R: The next morning the people got up early. They offered burnt offerings and brought fellowship offerings. They sat down to eat and drink. Then they got up and began to party wildly.

es.L: Y se levantaron temprano al día siguiente, y ofrecieron holocaustos y presentaron sacrificios de paz. Y se sentó el pueblo a comer y a beber, y se levantaron a divertirse.
es.B: Al día siguiente madrugaron para ofrecer holocaustos y presentar sacrificios de paz. Luego el pueblo se sentó a comer y a beber, y se levantó para entregarse al desenfreno.
es.R: A la mañana siguiente, el pueblo se levantó temprano. Ofrecieron holocaustos y presentaron sacrificios de paz. Se sentaron a comer y a beber. Después se levantaron y empezaron una fiesta sin control.

fr.L: Et ils se levèrent tôt le lendemain, et ils offrirent des holocaustes et présentèrent des sacrifices de communion. Et le peuple s’assit pour manger et pour boire, et ils se levèrent pour se divertir.
fr.B: Le lendemain, ils se levèrent de bonne heure pour offrir des holocaustes et présenter des sacrifices de communion. Puis le peuple s’assit pour manger et boire, et se leva pour se livrer à la débauche.
fr.R: Le lendemain matin, le peuple s’est levé tôt. Ils ont offert des holocaustes et apporté des sacrifices de communion. Ils se sont assis pour manger et boire. Puis ils se sont levés et ont fait une fête sans aucune retenue.

sw.L: Na wakaamka mapema siku iliyofuata, wakatoa sadaka za kuteketezwa, wakaleta sadaka za amani. Na watu wakaketi kula na kunywa, wakainuka kucheza.
sw.B: Kesho yake waliamka mapema, wakatoa sadaka za kuteketezwa na kuleta sadaka za amani. Kisha watu wakaketi kula na kunywa, wakainuka kufanya sherehe za ufisadi.
sw.R: Kesho yake asubuhi watu waliamka mapema. Walitoa sadaka za kuteketezwa, wakaleta sadaka za amani. Wakaketi kula na kunywa. Kisha wakainuka, wakaanza kusherehekea bila mipaka.

vi.L: Hôm sau, họ dậy sớm, dâng các của lễ thiêu và đem đến các tế lễ bình an. Rồi dân chúng ngồi xuống ăn uống, và đứng dậy vui chơi.
vi.B: Sáng hôm sau, họ dậy sớm dâng các của lễ thiêu và đem đến các tế lễ bình an. Dân chúng ngồi xuống ăn uống, rồi đứng dậy vui chơi trác táng.
vi.R: Sáng hôm sau, dân chúng dậy sớm. Họ dâng các của lễ thiêu và đem đến các tế lễ bình an. Họ ngồi xuống ăn uống. Rồi họ đứng dậy, vui chơi cuồng loạn.

ko.L: 그리고 그들은 이튿날 일찍 일어나 번제를 올려 드리고 화목제를 가져왔다. 그리고 백성은 앉아서 먹고 마셨고, 일어나서 놀았다.
ko.B: 이튿날 그들은 일찍 일어나 번제를 바치고 화목제를 드렸다. 그러고 나서 백성은 앉아서 먹고 마시고, 일어나서 흥청거리며 뛰놀았다.
ko.R: 이튿날 아침에 백성은 일찍 일어났다. 그들은 번제를 바치고 화목제를 드렸다. 그리고 앉아서 먹고 마셨다. 그다음에는 일어나서 마구 떠들며 놀았다.

decisions.choice: to play: to revel, with loud and unrestrained celebration
decisions.reason: The verb means to laugh, play or make sport. It is used of Isaac caressing Rebekah (Genesis 26:8) and of mocking (Genesis 39:14, 17). Here it goes with the dancing of verse 19 and the people "broken loose" of verse 25: wild feasting before the idol, which may have included sexual play. Paul quotes this verse in 1 Corinthians 10:7 as a warning against idolatry, and warns against sexual immorality in the next verse.

decisions.choice: burnt offerings, peace offerings, eating and drinking: a twisted copy of the covenant meal
decisions.reason: When the covenant was made, Israel offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and the elders ate and drank in God's presence (24:5, 11). Now the same acts are done before the calf.

decisions.choice: revel / party wildly
decisions.reason: "Play" sounds like children's games in English. Balanced says "revel" and Readable "party wildly" for the noisy celebration meant (m1). Literal keeps "play". Balanced and Readable say "fellowship offerings", Literal "peace offerings".

decisions.choice: "entregarse al desenfreno" (B); "una fiesta sin control" (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, "jugar" (play) would sound like children's games; Balanced and Readable say what kind of celebration it was (m1). Literal says "divertirse", which keeps the plain sense of the verb.

decisions.choice: "se livrer à la débauche" (B); "une fête sans aucune retenue" (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, "jouer" would sound like children's games; Balanced and Readable say what kind of celebration it was (m1), Literal keeps "se divertir".

decisions.choice: "화목제" for the peace offerings
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet: the *shelamim* are "화목제" at every level, in Exodus as in Leviticus. Recorded once for these chapters.

decisions.choice: "흥청거리며 뛰놀았다" (B); "마구 떠들며 놀았다" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb means loud, unrestrained revelry (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps the plain "놀았다", as the English Literal keeps "play", and Balanced and Readable say what kind of play it was.

decisions.choice: "của lễ thiêu"; "tế lễ bình an"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch terms note's words for the burnt offering and the peace offering, used through these chapters.

decisions.choice: "vui chơi trác táng" (Balanced); "vui chơi cuồng loạn" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The sense of unrestrained revelry (meaning decision); Literal keeps the plain "vui chơi".

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה לֶךְ־רֵ֕ד כִּ֚י שִׁחֵ֣ת עַמְּךָ֔ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱלֵ֖יתָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, go, go down, for has acted corruptly your people whom you brought up from [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, "Go, go down, for your people whom you brought up from the land of Egypt have acted corruptly.
en.B: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "Go down at once! Your people, whom you brought up from the land of Egypt, have acted corruptly.
en.R: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told Moses, "Hurry back down! Your people, the ones you led out of Egypt, have done something terrible.

es.L: Y habló {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Moisés: «Ve, baja, porque se ha corrompido tu pueblo, que hiciste subir de la tierra de Egipto.
es.B: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dijo a Moisés: «¡Baja ahora mismo! Tu pueblo, el que sacaste de la tierra de Egipto, se ha corrompido.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «¡Baja enseguida! Tu pueblo, el que sacaste de Egipto, ha hecho algo terrible.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} parla à Moïse : « Va, descends, car ton peuple, que tu as fait monter du pays d’Égypte, s’est corrompu.
fr.B: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « Descends immédiatement ! Ton peuple, que tu as fait monter du pays d’Égypte, s’est corrompu.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse : « Dépêche-toi de redescendre ! Ton peuple, ceux que tu as fait sortir d’Égypte, a fait quelque chose de terrible.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akanena na Musa, "Nenda, shuka, kwa maana watu wako uliowapandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri wamejiharibu.
sw.B: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Shuka sasa hivi! Watu wako, uliowapandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri, wamejiharibu.
sw.R: Kisha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa, "Shuka haraka! Watu wako, wale uliowatoa Misri, wamefanya jambo baya sana.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Hãy đi, hãy xuống, vì dân của ngươi mà ngươi đã đem lên khỏi xứ Ai Cập đã làm điều bại hoại.
vi.B: Bấy giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Hãy xuống ngay! Dân của con, là dân con đã đem lên khỏi xứ Ai Cập, đã làm điều bại hoại.
vi.R: Bấy giờ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Hãy mau xuống núi! Dân của con, là dân con đã dẫn ra khỏi Ai Cập, đã làm một điều tồi tệ.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "가거라, 내려가거라. 네가 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 올린 네 백성이 타락했다.
ko.B: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "어서 내려가거라. 네가 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 올린 네 백성이 타락했다.
ko.R: 그때 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "빨리 내려가거라. 네가 이집트에서 데리고 나온 네 백성이 끔찍한 짓을 저질렀다.

decisions.choice: your people, whom you brought up: God speaks of them as Moses' people
decisions.reason: God has called Israel "my people" (3:7, 10; 5:1). Here he calls them Moses' people, whom Moses brought up, the very words the people used of Moses in verse 1. In verse 11 Moses answers that they are God's people, whom God brought out.

decisions.choice: acted corruptly: ruined themselves, done what is destructive
decisions.reason: The verb means to spoil or ruin. It is used of the earth corrupted before the flood (Genesis 6:11-12) and of this same event in Deuteronomy 9:12.

decisions.choice: Go down at once / Hurry back down
decisions.reason: The two verbs "go, go down" press for haste; Balanced and Readable show it with "at once" and "hurry". Readable says "done something terrible" for "acted corruptly".

source.text: סָ֣רוּ מַהֵ֗ר מִן־הַדֶּ֨רֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֔ם עָשׂ֣וּ לָהֶ֔ם עֵ֖גֶל מַסֵּכָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁתַּֽחֲווּ־לוֹ֙ וַיִּזְבְּחוּ־ל֔וֹ וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ אֵ֤לֶּה אֱלֹהֶ֨יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶֽעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: They have turned aside quickly from the way which I commanded them. They have made for themselves a calf of cast metal and have bowed down to it and have sacrificed to it and have said, these [are] your gods, Israel, who brought you up from [the] land of Egypt.

en.L: They have turned aside quickly from the way that I commanded them. They have made for themselves a calf of cast metal and have bowed down to it and sacrificed to it and said, 'These [are] your gods, O Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt.'"
en.B: So soon they have left the path I laid down for them! They have cast a metal calf for themselves, bowed down before it, offered sacrifices to it, and declared, 'Israel, these are your gods, who brought you up from the land of Egypt!'"
en.R: They have been quick to stop doing what I commanded them. They have made themselves a calf out of melted metal. They have bowed down to it and offered sacrifices to it. They say, 'Israel, here are your gods who brought you out of Egypt!'"

es.L: Se han apartado pronto del camino que yo les mandé. Se han hecho un becerro de metal fundido, y se han postrado ante él y le han ofrecido sacrificios, y han dicho: “Estos [son] tus dioses, Israel, que te hicieron subir de la tierra de Egipto”».
es.B: ¡Qué pronto han dejado el camino que yo les señalé! Se han fundido un becerro de metal, se han postrado ante él, le han ofrecido sacrificios y han declarado: “¡Israel, estos son tus dioses, los que te sacaron de la tierra de Egipto!”».
es.R: Muy pronto dejaron de hacer lo que yo les mandé. Se han hecho un becerro de metal fundido. Se han inclinado ante él y le han ofrecido sacrificios. Dicen: “¡Israel, aquí están tus dioses, los que te sacaron de Egipto!”».

fr.L: Ils se sont vite détournés du chemin que je leur avais prescrit. Ils se sont fait un veau de métal fondu, et ils se sont prosternés devant lui, et ils lui ont offert des sacrifices, et ils ont dit : “Voici tes dieux, Israël, qui t’ont fait monter du pays d’Égypte.” »
fr.B: Ils n’ont pas tardé à quitter le chemin que je leur avais tracé ! Ils se sont fondu un veau de métal, ils se sont prosternés devant lui, lui ont offert des sacrifices et ont déclaré : “Israël, voici tes dieux, qui t’ont fait monter du pays d’Égypte !” »
fr.R: Ils ont vite cessé de faire ce que je leur avais commandé. Ils se sont fabriqué un veau en métal fondu. Ils se sont inclinés devant lui et lui ont offert des sacrifices. Ils disent : “Israël, voici tes dieux qui t’ont fait sortir d’Égypte !” »

sw.L: Wamegeuka upesi kutoka njia niliyowaamuru. Wamejifanyia ndama wa chuma kilichoyeyushwa, nao wamemsujudia na kumtolea dhabihu, na kusema, 'Hawa [ndio] miungu yako, Israeli, waliokupandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri.'"
sw.B: Upesi mno wameiacha njia niliyowawekea! Wamejitengenezea ndama wa chuma kilichoyeyushwa, wakamsujudia, wakamtolea dhabihu, na kutangaza, 'Ee Israeli, hawa ndio miungu yako waliokupandisha kutoka nchi ya Misri!'"
sw.R: Wameacha haraka kufanya yale niliyowaamuru. Wamejitengenezea ndama kwa chuma kilichoyeyushwa. Wamemsujudia na kumtolea dhabihu. Wanasema, 'Ee Israeli, tazama miungu yako iliyokutoa Misri!'"

vi.L: Chúng đã vội lìa bỏ con đường mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho chúng. Chúng đã làm cho mình một con bò con [bằng kim loại] đúc, cúi lạy nó, dâng tế lễ cho nó và nói: 'Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, đây [là] các thần của ngươi, là các thần đã đem ngươi lên khỏi xứ Ai Cập.'"
vi.B: Chúng đã vội bỏ con đường {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã truyền cho chúng! Chúng đã đúc cho mình một con bò con bằng kim loại, cúi lạy nó, dâng tế lễ cho nó và tuyên bố: 'Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, đây là các thần của ngươi, là các thần đã đem ngươi lên khỏi xứ Ai Cập!'"
vi.R: Chúng đã vội thôi làm theo những điều {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} truyền dạy. Chúng đã làm cho mình một con bò con bằng kim loại nấu chảy. Chúng cúi lạy nó và dâng tế lễ cho nó. Chúng nói: 'Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, đây là các thần của ngươi, là các thần đã đem ngươi ra khỏi Ai Cập!'"

ko.L: 그들이 내가 그들에게 명령한 길에서 빨리 벗어났다. 그들이 자기들을 위하여 부어 만든 송아지를 만들고, 그것에게 절하고 그것에게 제사를 드리며 말했다. '이스라엘아, 이것들이 너를 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 올린 너의 신들이다.'"
ko.B: 그들은 내가 명령한 길에서 이렇게 빨리 벗어나 버렸다. 그들은 금속을 부어 송아지를 만들고는, 그 앞에 절하고 제물을 바치며 '이스라엘아, 이것이 너를 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 올린 너의 신들이다!' 하고 외쳤다."
ko.R: 그들은 벌써 내가 명령한 것을 지키지 않고 있다. 그들은 녹인 금속으로 송아지를 만들었다. 그리고 그것에게 절하고 제물을 바쳤다. 그들은 '이스라엘아, 이것이 너를 이집트에서 데리고 나온 너의 신들이다!' 하고 말한다."

decisions.choice: turned aside quickly from the way I commanded: the covenant broken within weeks
decisions.reason: God had just commanded, "You shall have no other gods before me" and "You shall not make for yourself a carved image" (20:3-4), and "gods of gold you shall not make" (20:23). The people promised to keep his words (24:3, 7), and before Moses came down they had broken them.

decisions.choice: turned aside from the way: stopped living as God commanded
decisions.reason: The way is the path of life God laid out in his commands (Deuteronomy 9:12, 16; 31:29).

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת־הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה עַם־קְשֵׁה־עֹ֖רֶף הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh to Moses, I have seen the people this, and look, a people stiff of neck [is] it.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "I have seen this people, and look, a stiff-necked people it [is].
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} went on to say to Moses, "I have seen what this people is like. They are a stiff-necked people.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses, "I have been watching these people. They are stubborn and refuse to obey.

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} a Moisés: «He visto a este pueblo, y he aquí que es un pueblo duro de cerviz.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} siguió diciendo a Moisés: «Ya he visto cómo es este pueblo. Es un pueblo de dura cerviz.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dijo a Moisés: «He estado observando a esta gente. Son tercos y se niegan a obedecer.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit à Moïse : « J’ai vu ce peuple, et voici, c’est un peuple à la nuque raide.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit encore à Moïse : « J’ai vu ce qu’est ce peuple : c’est un peuple à la nuque raide.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a dit à Moïse : « J’observe ce peuple depuis un moment. Ils sont têtus et refusent d’obéir.

sw.L: Na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akamwambia Musa, "Nimewaona watu hawa, na tazama, ni watu wenye shingo ngumu.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaendelea kumwambia Musa, "Nimeona jinsi watu hawa walivyo. Ni watu wenye shingo ngumu.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimwambia Musa, "Nimekuwa nikiwatazama watu hawa. Ni wakaidi, na wanakataa kutii.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Ta đã thấy dân này, và kìa, nó [là] một dân cứng cổ.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} lại phán với Môi-se: "Ta đã thấy dân này là thế nào. Đó là một dân cứng cổ.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán với Môi-se: "Ta đã nhìn thấy dân này. Chúng thật bướng bỉnh và không chịu vâng lời.

ko.L: 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 이 백성을 보았다. 보아라, 그들은 목이 뻣뻣한 백성이다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 또 말씀하셨다. "내가 이 백성이 어떠한지 보았다. 그들은 목이 뻣뻣한 백성이다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 모세에게 말씀하셨다. "내가 이 백성을 지켜보았다. 그들은 고집이 세고 내 말을 듣지 않는다.

decisions.choice: stiff-necked: stubborn, refusing to be led
decisions.reason: The picture is of an ox or donkey that stiffens its neck against the yoke or the driver's lead. Israel is called this again in 33:3, 5 and 34:9, and in Deuteronomy 9:6, 13.

decisions.choice: stubborn and refuse to obey
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1). Literal and Balanced keep "stiff-necked", which is still understood in English.

decisions.choice: "duro de cerviz" (L), "de dura cerviz" (B), here and in 33:3, 5 and 34:9
decisions.reason: "Cerviz" (the nape of the neck) is the word Spanish uses in this idiom, and it is still understood of stubborn people. Literal keeps the Hebrew order, "stiff of neck". Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "un peuple à la nuque raide", here and in 33:3, 5 and 34:9
decisions.reason: French keeps the picture of the animal stiffening its neck (m1); "la nuque raide" is the form in which French still uses it of stubborn people. Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "watu wenye shingo ngumu", here and in 33:3, 5 and 34:9
decisions.reason: Swahili keeps the picture of a hard, unbending neck (m1), which Swahili readers know as an image of stubbornness. Readable says "wakaidi", as the English says "stubborn".

decisions.choice: "목이 뻣뻣한" (L, B); "고집이 세고 내 말을 듣지 않는다" (R)
decisions.reason: The picture of an ox that will not bend its neck to the yoke (meaning decision m1) is kept at Literal and Balanced, where Korean readers can follow it; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "cứng cổ" (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese has the same picture ("cứng cổ", stubborn) as the Hebrew, so Literal and Balanced keep it; Readable says what it means, as the English does.

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ הַנִּ֣יחָה לִּ֔י וְיִֽחַר־אַפִּ֥י בָהֶ֖ם וַאֲכַלֵּ֑ם וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה אוֹתְךָ֖ לְג֥וֹי גָּדֽוֹל׃

records.literal_gloss: And now leave me alone, that may burn my anger against them and I may consume them, and I will make you into a nation great.

en.L: And now, let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} alone, that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger may burn hot against them and I may consume them; and I will make you into a great nation."
en.B: So now let {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} alone, so that {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath can burn hot against them and I can put an end to them. Then I will make you into a great nation."
en.R: Now do not try to stop {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I am so angry with them that I will destroy them. Then I will make your family into a great nation."

es.L: Y ahora, déjame, para que se encienda {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira contra ellos y los consuma; y de ti haré una nación grande».
es.B: Así que ahora déjame, para que {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor arda contra ellos y acabe con ellos. Luego haré de ti una gran nación».
es.R: Ahora no {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} detengas. Estoy tan enojado con ellos que los voy a destruir. Después haré de tu familia una gran nación».

fr.L: Et maintenant, laisse-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, que {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère s’enflamme contre eux et que je les consume ; et je ferai de toi une grande nation. »
fr.B: Maintenant donc, laisse-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} faire : que {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur s’embrase contre eux et que j’en finisse avec eux ! Ensuite, je ferai de toi une grande nation. »
fr.R: N’essaie pas de {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}arrêter. Je suis si en colère contre eux que je vais les détruire. Ensuite, je ferai de ta famille une grande nation. »

sw.L: Basi sasa niache, ili hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} iwake juu yao, niwamalize; {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakufanya wewe kuwa taifa kubwa."
sw.B: Basi sasa niache, ili ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} iwawakie, niwakomeshe kabisa. Kisha nitakufanya wewe kuwa taifa kubwa."
sw.R: Sasa usijaribu kunizuia. Nimewakasirikia sana hata nitawaangamiza. Kisha nitaifanya jamaa yako kuwa taifa kubwa."

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, hãy để {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yên, để cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nổi phừng lên với chúng và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tiêu diệt chúng; rồi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho ngươi thành một dân lớn."
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, hãy để {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} yên, để cơn thịnh nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bùng cháy nghịch lại chúng và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} tiêu diệt chúng. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho con thành một dân lớn."
vi.R: Bây giờ đừng cố ngăn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. Ta giận chúng đến nỗi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tiêu diệt chúng. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho dòng dõi con thành một dân lớn."

ko.L: 이제 나를 내버려 두어라. 내 분노가 그들에게 타올라 내가 그들을 없애 버리겠다. 그리고 너를 큰 민족으로 만들겠다."
ko.B: 그러니 이제 나를 말리지 말아라. 내 진노가 그들에게 불붙어, 내가 그들을 없애 버리겠다. 그 대신 너를 큰 민족으로 만들겠다."
ko.R: 이제 나를 막으려 하지 말아라. 나는 그들에게 너무나 화가 나서 그들을 없애 버리겠다. 그리고 네 집안을 큰 민족으로 만들겠다."

decisions.choice: let me alone: God leaves room for Moses to plead
decisions.reason: God tells Moses to leave him alone, as if Moses could hold him back. The words announce judgment, yet they also invite the plea that follows (verses 11-13). Later Scripture remembers that Moses "stood in the breach" before God to turn away his wrath (Psalm 106:23; Deuteronomy 9:19-20, 25-26).

decisions.choice: I will make you into a great nation: the promise to Abraham, offered to Moses
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham, "I will make you into a great nation" (Genesis 12:2). Here God offers to begin again with Moses alone. Moses refuses, appealing to the promise to Abraham, Isaac and Israel (verse 13).

decisions.choice: do not try to stop me ... your family
decisions.reason: Readable says what "let me alone" means here, and "your family" for "you", since a nation would come from Moses' descendants.

source.text: וַיְחַ֣ל מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֖י יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֑יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָמָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ יֶחֱרֶ֤ה אַפְּךָ֙ בְּעַמֶּ֔ךָ אֲשֶׁ֤ר הוֹצֵ֨אתָ֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּכֹ֥חַ גָּד֖וֹל וּבְיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And implored Moses [the] face of Yahweh his God and said, why, Yahweh, does burn your anger against your people whom you brought out from [the] land of Egypt with power great and with a hand strong?

en.L: And Moses implored the face of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God and said, "Why, O {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, does {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger burn against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} brought out from the land of Egypt with great power and with a strong hand?
en.B: But Moses sought the favor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God. "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}," he said, "why should {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} anger blaze against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people? You brought them out of the land of Egypt by great power and a strong hand.
en.R: But Moses begged {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God to be kind. He said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} so angry with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people? You used {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} great power and strength to bring them out of Egypt.

es.L: Y Moisés imploró el rostro {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} su Dios, y dijo: «¿Por qué, oh {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, se enciende {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira contra {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo, que sacaste de la tierra de Egipto con gran poder y con mano fuerte?
es.B: Pero Moisés buscó el favor {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} su Dios. «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}», dijo, «¿por qué ha de arder {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira contra {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} propio pueblo? Tú los sacaste de la tierra de Egipto con gran poder y mano fuerte.
es.R: Pero Moisés le rogó {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} su Dios que tuviera bondad. Le dijo: «{{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, ¿por qué estás tan enojado con {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo? Usaste {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} gran poder y {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fuerza para sacarlos de Egipto.

fr.L: Et Moïse implora la face {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} son Dieu, et dit : « Pourquoi, ô {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère s’enflamme-t-elle contre {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple, que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as fait sortir du pays d’Égypte avec une grande puissance et d’une main forte ?
fr.B: Mais Moïse chercha à apaiser {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} son Dieu. « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, dit-il, pourquoi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère s’embraserait-elle contre {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} propre peuple ? C’est {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} qui l’as fait sortir du pays d’Égypte avec une grande puissance et une main forte.
fr.R: Mais Moïse a supplié {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} son Dieu d’être bon. Il lui a dit : « {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, pourquoi es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} tellement en colère contre {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple ? Tu as utilisé {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} grande puissance et {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} force pour le faire sortir d’Égypte.

sw.L: Naye Musa akausihi uso wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wake, akasema, "Kwa nini, Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} inawaka juu ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, uliowatoa kutoka nchi ya Misri kwa nguvu nyingi na kwa mkono hodari?
sw.B: Lakini Musa akatafuta kibali cha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wake, akasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa nini hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} iwawakie watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} mwenyewe? Wewe ndiye uliyewatoa katika nchi ya Misri kwa uweza mkuu na mkono wenye nguvu.
sw.R: Lakini Musa alimwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wake awe na huruma. Akasema, "Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, kwa nini umewakasirikia watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} kiasi hiki? Ulitumia nguvu {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} kuu kuwatoa Misri.

vi.L: Môi-se nài xin trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của mình và nói: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, sao cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại nổi phừng lên với dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là dân mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đem ra khỏi xứ Ai Cập bằng quyền năng lớn và bằng tay mạnh mẽ?
vi.B: Nhưng Môi-se tìm ơn trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của mình. Ông thưa: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, sao cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại bùng cháy nghịch lại chính dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}? Chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã đem họ ra khỏi xứ Ai Cập bằng quyền năng lớn và cánh tay mạnh mẽ.
vi.R: Nhưng Môi-se khẩn xin {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời của mình thương xót. Ông thưa: "Lạy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, sao {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại giận dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến thế? Chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã dùng quyền năng lớn lao và sức mạnh của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà đem họ ra khỏi Ai Cập.

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 자기 하나님의 얼굴을 구하며 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 어찌하여 주님께서 큰 능력과 강한 손으로 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 내신 주님의 백성에게 주님의 분노를 태우십니까?
ko.B: 그러나 모세는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 자기 하나님께 은혜를 구하며 말했다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 어찌하여 주님의 백성에게 그토록 진노하십니까? 그들은 주님께서 큰 능력과 강한 손으로 이집트 땅에서 이끌어 내신 백성이 아닙니까?
ko.R: 그러나 모세는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}} 자기 하나님께 은혜를 베풀어 달라고 간절히 빌었다. "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여, 어찌하여 주님의 백성에게 이렇게 화를 내십니까? 주님께서 큰 힘과 능력으로 그들을 이집트에서 데리고 나오시지 않았습니까?

decisions.choice: implored the face of Yahweh: sought his favor
decisions.reason: The phrase means to soften someone's face, that is, to seek the favor of someone who is angry (1 Samuel 13:12; 1 Kings 13:6). It is a different verb from the "entreat" of the plague stories (8:4).

decisions.choice: your people, whom you brought out: Moses hands God's words back to him
decisions.reason: God had called them Moses' people, whom Moses brought up (verse 7). Moses answers that they are God's people, and that God brought them out by his own great power and strong hand (6:1; 13:9).

decisions.choice: implored (Literal); sought the favor of (Balanced); begged ... to be kind (Readable)
decisions.reason: This verb is not the one rendered "entreat", "plead with" and "pray to" in the plague stories, so the levels use other words that bring out the asking for favor (m1).

decisions.choice: "chercha à apaiser" (sought to appease)
decisions.reason: French has no natural phrase for "seek the favor of" someone; "chercher à apaiser" says what Moses' pleading aimed at, God's anger turned to favor (m1).

decisions.choice: Moses speaks to God in 합쇼체, calling him "주님" and himself "저"
decisions.reason: As the Genesis and Pentateuch term sheets: people pray in 합쇼체 and address God as 주님; "당신" would sound cold or rude in Korean. The vocative of the divine name is "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}여". Recorded once for these chapters.

decisions.choice: Moses prays "Lạy CHÚA", calls God "Ngài" and says "con" for himself
decisions.reason: The prayer forms the Genesis terms note sets for people speaking to God; kept through Moses' prayers in chapters 32-34.

source.text: לָמָּה֩ יֹאמְר֨וּ מִצְרַ֜יִם לֵאמֹ֗ר בְּרָעָ֤ה הֽוֹצִיאָם֙ לַהֲרֹ֤ג אֹתָם֙ בֶּֽהָרִ֔ים וּ֨לְכַלֹּתָ֔ם מֵעַ֖ל פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֑ה שׁ֚וּב מֵחֲר֣וֹן אַפֶּ֔ךָ וְהִנָּחֵ֥ם עַל־הָרָעָ֖ה לְעַמֶּֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Why should say Egypt, saying, with evil he brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and to consume them from upon [the] face of the ground? Turn from [the] burning of your anger and relent concerning the harm to your people.

en.L: Why should Egypt say, 'With evil [intent] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and to consume them from upon the face of the ground'? Turn from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} burning anger, and relent concerning the harm to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.
en.B: Why should the Egyptians say, 'He brought them out to do them harm, to kill them among the mountains and put an end to them on the face of the earth'? Turn from {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} fierce anger, and relent from the harm {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} mean to bring on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.
en.R: Do not let the Egyptians say, 'He led them out only to hurt them. He wanted to kill them in the mountains and destroy every one of them.' Please stop being so angry! Change {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} mind, and do not bring this harm on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people.

es.L: ¿Por qué ha de decir Egipto: “Con mala [intención] los sacó, para matarlos en los montes y para consumirlos de sobre la faz de la tierra”? Vuélvete del ardor de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira, y desiste del mal contra {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo.
es.B: ¿Por qué han de decir los egipcios: “Los sacó para hacerles daño, para matarlos entre los montes y borrarlos de la faz de la tierra”? Aparta el ardor de {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ira y desiste del mal que piensas traer sobre {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo.
es.R: No dejes que los egipcios digan: “Los sacó solo para hacerles daño. Quería matarlos en los montes y acabar con todos ellos”. ¡Por favor, deja de estar tan enojado! Cambia de parecer, y no traigas este mal sobre {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} pueblo.

fr.L: Pourquoi l’Égypte dirait-elle : “C’est avec une mauvaise [intention] qu’il les a fait sortir, pour les tuer dans les montagnes et pour les consumer de dessus la face du sol” ? Reviens de l’ardeur de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère, et renonce au mal [prévu] contre {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple.
fr.B: Pourquoi les Égyptiens diraient-ils : “Il les a fait sortir pour leur faire du mal, pour les tuer dans les montagnes et les faire disparaître de la surface de la terre” ? Reviens de {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} colère ardente, et renonce au mal que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} veux faire à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple.
fr.R: Ne laisse pas les Égyptiens dire : “Il les a fait sortir seulement pour leur faire du mal. Il voulait les tuer dans les montagnes et les faire tous disparaître.” Je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}en prie, ne sois plus en colère ! Change d’avis, et ne fais pas ce mal à {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} peuple.

sw.L: Kwa nini Misri iseme, 'Kwa nia mbaya aliwatoa, ili awaue milimani na kuwaangamiza kutoka juu ya uso wa ardhi'? Geuka kutoka ukali wa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, ughairi kuhusu madhara juu ya watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.B: Kwa nini Wamisri waseme, 'Aliwatoa ili awadhuru, awaue katikati ya milima na kuwafuta kutoka uso wa dunia'? Acha hasira {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} kali, ughairi madhara uliyokusudia kuwaletea watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}.
sw.R: Usiwaache Wamisri waseme, 'Aliwatoa ili tu awadhuru. Alitaka kuwaua milimani na kuwamaliza wote.' Tafadhali, usiendelee kukasirika hivyo! Badili nia yako, usiwaletee watu {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} madhara haya.

vi.L: Sao để người Ai Cập nói rằng: 'Ngài đã đem họ ra với [ý] xấu, để giết họ trên núi và tiêu diệt họ khỏi mặt đất'? Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nguôi cơn giận phừng phừng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và đổi ý về tai họa [định giáng] trên dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Sao lại để người Ai Cập nói: 'Ngài đem họ ra là để hại họ, để giết họ giữa núi non và xóa họ khỏi mặt đất'? Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nguôi cơn giận dữ dội, và đổi ý không giáng tai họa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} định giáng trên dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Xin đừng để người Ai Cập nói: 'Ngài dẫn họ ra chỉ để hại họ. Ngài muốn giết họ trên núi và tiêu diệt hết họ.' Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đừng giận nữa! Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đổi ý, và đừng giáng tai họa này trên dân của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 어찌하여 이집트 사람들이 '그가 악한 [뜻으로] 그들을 이끌어 내어 산에서 죽이고 땅 위에서 없애 버렸다'고 말하게 하시겠습니까? 주님의 타오르는 분노를 돌이키시고, 주님의 백성에게 내리시려던 재앙을 거두어 주십시오.
ko.B: 어찌하여 이집트 사람들이 '그가 그들을 해치려고, 산에서 죽이고 이 땅 위에서 없애 버리려고 이끌어 냈다'고 말하게 하시겠습니까? 주님의 불타는 진노를 거두시고, 주님의 백성에게 내리시려던 재앙을 돌이켜 주십시오.
ko.R: 이집트 사람들이 '그들의 하나님이 그들을 해치려고 데리고 나갔다. 산에서 그들을 죽여서 하나도 남기지 않으려고 그랬다' 하고 말하지 않게 해 주십시오. 제발 노여움을 푸십시오. 마음을 돌이키셔서, 주님의 백성에게 그런 재앙을 내리지 마십시오.

decisions.choice: with evil ... the harm: one word, used twice
decisions.reason: The same word means "evil" and "harm" or "disaster". Moses asks God not to do the "harm" that would let the Egyptians say he brought Israel out with "evil" intent: God's name among the nations is at stake (compare 9:16; Numbers 14:13-16).

decisions.choice: relent: change course, turn from what was intended
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in verse 14, where the note explains it.

decisions.choice: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: "Egypt" here means the people of Egypt; Balanced and Readable say "the Egyptians". Readable says "Change your mind" for "relent", as in verse 14.

decisions.choice: "desiste del mal" (L, B); "cambia de parecer" (R), as in verse 14
decisions.reason: "Arrepentirse", the older rendering, now suggests turning away from sin, which is not what is asked of God here; "desistir" says that God holds back the harm he spoke of.

decisions.choice: "ughairi" (L, B); "badili nia yako" (R), as in verse 14
decisions.reason: "Kughairi" is to give up a purpose one had set; "kujuta" (regret) and "kutubu" (repent) would suggest God had done wrong.

decisions.choice: "악한 [뜻으로] ... 재앙" (L); "해치려고 ... 재앙" (B, R)
alternatives: the same Korean word in both places
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one word twice, evil intent and harm (meaning decision m1). Korean has no single word that serves both clauses naturally, so the link is lost; it is kept in the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: "Ngài" opens the quoted words with no span
decisions.reason: A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital, as the Vietnamese style guide says; mid-sentence it takes the deity_pronoun span.

source.text: זְכֹ֡ר לְאַבְרָהָם֩ לְיִצְחָ֨ק וּלְיִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֣עְתָּ לָהֶם֮ בָּךְ֒ וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַרְבֶּה֙ אֶֽת־זַרְעֲכֶ֔ם כְּכוֹכְבֵ֖י הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וְכָל־הָאָ֨רֶץ הַזֹּ֜את אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֗רְתִּי אֶתֵּן֙ לְזַרְעֲכֶ֔ם וְנָחֲל֖וּ לְעֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself and said to them, I will multiply your offspring like [the] stars of the heavens, and all the land this which I have said I will give to your offspring, and they will possess [it] forever.

en.L: Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants, to whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} swore by {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} and said to them, 'I will multiply your offspring like the stars of the heavens, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your offspring, and they shall possess [it] forever.'"
en.B: Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, who served {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You swore to them by {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} and told them, 'I will make your descendants as many as the stars in the sky. All this land I have spoken of I will give to your descendants, and it will be theirs for all time.'"
en.R: Remember {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You made them a promise and swore by {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}. You said, 'I will give you more descendants than there are stars in the sky. I will give your descendants all this land I promised, and it will belong to them forever.'"

es.L: Acuérdate de Abraham, de Isaac y de Israel, {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} siervos, a quienes juraste por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo y les dijiste: “Multiplicaré {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} descendencia como las estrellas de los cielos, y toda esta tierra de la que he hablado la daré a {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} descendencia, y la poseerán para siempre”».
es.B: Acuérdate de Abraham, de Isaac y de Israel, que {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} sirvieron. Tú les juraste por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo y les dijiste: “Haré a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} descendientes tan numerosos como las estrellas del cielo. Toda esta tierra de la que he hablado se la daré a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} descendientes, y será suya para siempre”».
es.R: Acuérdate de {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} siervos Abraham, Isaac y Jacob. Tú les hiciste una promesa y la juraste por {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} mismo. Les dijiste: “{{plural_you:Les|Os}} daré más descendientes que estrellas hay en el cielo. A {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} descendientes les daré toda esta tierra que prometí, y será de ellos para siempre”».

fr.L: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} d’Abraham, d’Isaac et d’Israël, {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} serviteurs, auxquels {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as juré par {{deity_pronoun:toi-même|Toi-même}}, et à qui {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as dit : “Je multiplierai votre descendance comme les étoiles des cieux, et tout ce pays dont j’ai parlé, je le donnerai à votre descendance, et ils [le] posséderont pour toujours.” »
fr.B: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} d’Abraham, d’Isaac et d’Israël, qui {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ont servi. Tu leur as juré par {{deity_pronoun:toi-même|Toi-même}}, en leur disant : “Je rendrai votre descendance aussi nombreuse que les étoiles du ciel. Tout ce pays dont j’ai parlé, je le donnerai à vos descendants, et il sera à eux pour toujours.” »
fr.R: Souviens-{{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} serviteurs Abraham, Isaac et Jacob. Tu leur as fait une promesse, et tu l’as jurée par {{deity_pronoun:toi-même|Toi-même}}. Tu leur as dit : “Je vous donnerai plus de descendants qu’il n’y a d’étoiles dans le ciel. Je donnerai à vos descendants tout ce pays que j’ai promis, et il leur appartiendra pour toujours.” »

sw.L: Wakumbuke Abrahamu, Isaka na Israeli, watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, uliowaapia kwa nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, ukawaambia, 'Nitauzidisha uzao wenu kama nyota za mbinguni, na nchi hii yote niliyoisema nitawapa uzao wenu, nao wataimiliki milele.'"
sw.B: Wakumbuke Abrahamu, Isaka na Israeli, waliokutumikia. Uliwaapia kwa nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}} na kuwaambia, 'Nitawafanya wazao wenu kuwa wengi kama nyota za angani. Nchi hii yote niliyoitaja nitawapa wazao wenu, nayo itakuwa mali yao siku zote.'"
sw.R: Wakumbuke watumishi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} Abrahamu, Isaka na Yakobo. Uliwapa ahadi, ukaiapia kwa nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}. Uliwaambia, 'Nitawapa wazao wengi kuliko nyota za angani. Nitawapa wazao wenu nchi hii yote niliyoahidi, nayo itakuwa yao milele.'"

vi.L: Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại Áp-ra-ham, Y-sác và Y-sơ-ra-ên, các đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là những người {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chỉ chính mình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà thề và phán với họ: 'Ta sẽ làm cho dòng dõi các ngươi đông như sao trên trời, và cả xứ này mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ban cho dòng dõi các ngươi, và họ sẽ chiếm hữu [nó] đời đời.'"
vi.B: Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại Áp-ra-ham, Y-sác và Y-sơ-ra-ên, là những người đã phục vụ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã chỉ chính mình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà thề với họ: 'Ta sẽ làm cho dòng dõi các ngươi đông như sao trên trời. Cả xứ này mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã nói, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ban cho dòng dõi các ngươi, và xứ ấy sẽ thuộc về họ mãi mãi.'"
vi.R: Xin {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nhớ lại các đầy tớ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} là Áp-ra-ham, Y-sác và Gia-cốp. Chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã hứa với họ và chỉ chính mình {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mà thề. Ngài đã phán: 'Ta sẽ cho các ngươi có con cháu đông hơn sao trên trời. Ta sẽ ban cho con cháu các ngươi cả xứ này như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã hứa, và xứ ấy sẽ thuộc về họ đời đời.'"

ko.L: 주님의 종들인 아브라함과 이삭과 이스라엘을 기억하여 주십시오. 주님께서는 그들에게 주님 자신을 두고 맹세하시며 말씀하셨습니다. '내가 너희 자손을 하늘의 별들처럼 많아지게 하고, 내가 말한 이 온 땅을 너희 자손에게 주어, 그들이 영원히 [그것을] 차지하게 하겠다.'"
ko.B: 주님을 섬긴 아브라함과 이삭과 이스라엘을 기억하여 주십시오. 주님께서는 친히 주님 자신을 두고 그들에게 맹세하시며 말씀하셨습니다. '내가 너희 자손을 하늘의 별처럼 많게 하겠다. 내가 말한 이 온 땅을 너희 자손에게 주어 영원히 그들의 것이 되게 하겠다.'"
ko.R: 주님의 종 아브라함과 이삭과 야곱을 기억해 주십시오. 주님께서는 그들에게 약속하시면서 주님 자신을 두고 맹세하셨습니다. '내가 너희에게 하늘의 별보다 더 많은 자손을 주겠다. 내가 약속한 이 온 땅을 너희 자손에게 주어서 영원히 그들의 것이 되게 하겠다.'"

decisions.choice: you swore by yourself ... like the stars: God's oath to the fathers
decisions.reason: After Abraham offered Isaac, God swore by himself to multiply his offspring like the stars of the heavens (Genesis 22:16-17; see also 15:5; 26:4). The land was promised to Abraham and his offspring (Genesis 12:7; 13:15; 28:13). With no one greater to swear by, God swore by himself (Hebrews 6:13).

decisions.choice: Israel: Jacob
decisions.reason: Israel is the name God gave Jacob (Genesis 35:10), and the people are named after him.

decisions.choice: Jacob
decisions.reason: Readable uses the patriarch's more familiar name, so readers do not confuse him with the people (m2).

decisions.choice: "chỉ chính mình Ngài mà thề" for "swore by yourself"
decisions.reason: The wording the Vietnamese Genesis 22:16 uses for the same oath, which Moses recalls here.

source.text: וַיִּנָּ֖חֶם יְהוָ֑ה עַל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לְעַמּֽוֹ׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And relented Yahweh concerning the harm which he had spoken to do to his people.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented concerning the harm that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken of doing to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.
en.B: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} relented from the harm {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would do to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} changed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mind. He did not do the harm {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would do to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

es.L: Y desistió {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} del mal que había dicho que haría a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo.
es.B: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} desistió del mal que había anunciado contra {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo.
es.R: Entonces {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} cambió de parecer. No le hizo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo el mal que había dicho que le haría.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} renonça au mal qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait parlé de faire à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple.
fr.B: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} renonça au mal qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait dit vouloir faire à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple.
fr.R: Alors {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a changé d’avis. Il n’a pas fait à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple le mal qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} avait annoncé.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaghairi kuhusu madhara aliyosema kuwatendea watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaghairi madhara aliyokuwa amesema atawaletea watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alibadili nia {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Hakuwaletea watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} madhara aliyokuwa amesema.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý về tai họa mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán sẽ làm cho dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý, không giáng tai họa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán sẽ giáng trên dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Vậy {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đổi ý. Ngài không giáng tai họa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã phán sẽ giáng trên dân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 자기 백성에게 내리시겠다고 말씀하신 재앙에 대하여 뜻을 돌이키셨다.
ko.B: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 자기 백성에게 내리겠다고 하신 재앙을 거두셨다.
ko.R: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 마음을 바꾸셨다. 그분은 자기 백성에게 내리겠다고 하신 재앙을 내리지 않으셨다.

decisions.choice: relented: God's response, told in human terms
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in Genesis 6:6 for God's regret. It means to change course or to turn from what was intended. The Bible says God does not change his mind as a human does (Numbers 23:19; 1 Samuel 15:29), yet it often says he relents when people turn or when someone pleads for them (Jeremiah 18:7-10; Jonah 3:10; Amos 7:3, 6). This does not mean God was mistaken or did not foresee events. It shows that he truly answers prayer: Moses pleaded, and the judgment threatened in verse 10 was not carried out.

decisions.choice: the harm he had spoken of: the destruction threatened in verse 10
decisions.reason: The word means harm or disaster here, not moral evil.

decisions.choice: changed his mind
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday phrase; Literal and Balanced say "relented". "Repented" is avoided at every level, since in English it suggests turning from sin.

decisions.choice: "renonça au mal" (L, B); "a changé d'avis" (R), as in verse 12
decisions.reason: "Se repentir" now suggests turning away from sin, which is not what the verse says of God; "renoncer à" says that he held back the harm he had spoken of.

source.text: וַיִּ֜פֶן וַיֵּ֤רֶד מֹשֶׁה֙ מִן־הָהָ֔ר וּשְׁנֵ֛י לֻחֹ֥ת הָעֵדֻ֖ת בְּיָד֑וֹ לֻחֹ֗ת כְּתֻבִים֙ מִשְּׁנֵ֣י עֶבְרֵיהֶ֔ם מִזֶּ֥ה וּמִזֶּ֖ה הֵ֥ם כְּתֻבִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And turned and went down Moses from the mountain, and [the] two tablets of the testimony [were] in his hand, tablets written on both their sides; on this and on this they [were] written.

en.L: And Moses turned and went down from the mountain, and the two tablets of the testimony [were] in his hand, tablets written on both their sides; on this [side] and on that [side] they were written.
en.B: Then Moses turned and went down from the mountain, holding the two tablets of the testimony. These tablets were written on both sides, on the one face and on the other.
en.R: Moses turned and went down the mountain. In his hands he carried the two stone tablets of the covenant. There was writing on both sides of them, front and back.

es.L: Y se volvió y descendió Moisés del monte, y las dos tablas del Testimonio [estaban] en su mano, tablas escritas por sus dos lados; por uno y por otro estaban escritas.
es.B: Entonces Moisés se volvió y bajó del monte con las dos tablas del Testimonio en la mano. Las tablas estaban escritas por los dos lados, por una cara y por la otra.
es.R: Moisés se dio la vuelta y bajó del monte. En las manos llevaba las dos tablas de piedra del pacto. Estaban escritas por los dos lados, por delante y por detrás.

fr.L: Et Moïse se tourna et descendit de la montagne, et les deux tablettes du Témoignage [étaient] dans sa main, des tablettes écrites sur leurs deux côtés ; sur l’un et sur l’autre elles étaient écrites.
fr.B: Puis Moïse se retourna et descendit de la montagne, tenant en main les deux tablettes du Témoignage. Ces tablettes étaient écrites des deux côtés, sur une face et sur l’autre.
fr.R: Moïse s’est retourné et il est descendu de la montagne. Il portait dans ses mains les deux tablettes de pierre de l’alliance. Elles étaient écrites des deux côtés, devant et derrière.

sw.L: Naye Musa akageuka, akashuka kutoka mlimani, na vibao viwili vya Ushuhuda [vilikuwa] mkononi mwake, vibao vilivyoandikwa pande zake zote mbili; upande huu na upande huu vilikuwa vimeandikwa.
sw.B: Kisha Musa akageuka, akashuka kutoka mlimani akiwa ameshika vibao viwili vya Ushuhuda. Vibao hivyo vilikuwa vimeandikwa pande zote mbili, mbele na nyuma.
sw.R: Musa aligeuka, akashuka mlimani. Mikononi mwake alibeba vibao viwili vya mawe vya agano. Vilikuwa vimeandikwa pande zote mbili, mbele na nyuma.

vi.L: Môi-se quay lại và đi xuống núi, hai bảng chứng ước ở trong tay ông, các bảng được viết cả hai mặt; mặt này và mặt kia đều được viết.
vi.B: Rồi Môi-se quay lại và đi xuống núi, tay cầm hai bảng chứng ước. Hai bảng này có chữ viết cả hai mặt, mặt trước và mặt sau.
vi.R: Môi-se quay lại và đi xuống núi. Tay ông cầm hai bảng đá giao ước. Cả hai mặt của các bảng đều có chữ, mặt trước và mặt sau.

ko.L: 그리고 모세가 돌아서서 산에서 내려왔는데, 증거판 둘이 그의 손에 [있었다]. 그 판은 양면에 글이 쓰여 있었으니, 이쪽에도 저쪽에도 쓰여 있었다.
ko.B: 모세는 돌아서서 증거판 두 개를 손에 들고 산에서 내려왔다. 그 판에는 양면에, 앞뒤로 글이 새겨져 있었다.
ko.R: 모세는 돌아서서 산을 내려왔다. 그의 손에는 언약을 새긴 돌판 두 개가 들려 있었다. 그 돌판에는 앞뒤 양쪽에 다 글이 쓰여 있었다.

decisions.choice: the tablets of the testimony: the stone tablets bearing the covenant
decisions.reason: These are the tablets God gave Moses in 31:18, written with the covenant words, God's witness to the covenant (25:16).

decisions.choice: written on both sides: the whole text, front and back
decisions.reason: Writing on both faces of a tablet was unusual. It may stress that the tablets were full and complete, with nothing to be added.

decisions.choice: the two stone tablets of the covenant
decisions.reason: As in 31:18, Readable says "of the covenant" for "of the testimony". It says "hands", since Moses carried two tablets.

decisions.choice: "les tablettes" (the tablets), here and in chapters 31-34
decisions.reason: "Les tables de la Loi" is the traditional French name, but "table" today first means a piece of furniture; "tablettes" says plainly that they were flat stones to write on.

source.text: וְהַ֨לֻּחֹ֔ת מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים הֵ֑מָּה וְהַמִּכְתָּ֗ב מִכְתַּ֤ב אֱלֹהִים֙ ה֔וּא חָר֖וּת עַל־הַלֻּחֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And the tablets [were the] work of God they, and the writing [was the] writing of God it, engraved on the tablets.

en.L: And the tablets, they [were] the work of God, and the writing, it [was] the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
en.B: God {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} had made the tablets, and the writing cut into them was God's own writing.
en.R: God had made the tablets. God had cut the words into them in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own writing.

es.L: Y las tablas, ellas [eran] obra de Dios, y la escritura, ella [era] escritura de Dios, grabada sobre las tablas.
es.B: Dios mismo había hecho las tablas, y la escritura grabada en ellas era la escritura de Dios.
es.R: Dios había hecho las tablas. Dios había grabado las palabras en ellas con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia letra.

fr.L: Et les tablettes, elles [étaient] l’œuvre de Dieu, et l’écriture, elle [était] l’écriture de Dieu, gravée sur les tablettes.
fr.B: Dieu {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} avait fait les tablettes, et l’écriture gravée sur elles était l’écriture de Dieu.
fr.R: C’est Dieu qui avait fait les tablettes. Dieu avait gravé les mots dessus de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} propre écriture.

sw.L: Na vibao hivyo, vilikuwa kazi ya Mungu, na maandishi hayo, yalikuwa maandishi ya Mungu, yaliyochongwa juu ya vibao.
sw.B: Mungu {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} ndiye aliyevitengeneza vibao hivyo, na maandishi yaliyochongwa juu yake yalikuwa mwandiko wa Mungu.
sw.R: Mungu alikuwa ametengeneza vibao hivyo. Mungu alichonga maneno juu yake kwa mwandiko {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

vi.L: Các bảng ấy [là] công việc của Đức Chúa Trời, và chữ viết [là] chữ viết của Đức Chúa Trời, được khắc trên các bảng.
vi.B: Chính Đức Chúa Trời đã làm các bảng ấy, và chữ khắc trên đó là chính chữ viết của Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời đã làm ra các bảng ấy. Chính Đức Chúa Trời đã khắc chữ lên đó bằng nét chữ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그 판들은 하나님께서 만드신 것이요, 그 글씨는 하나님의 글씨로서 판들 위에 새겨진 것이었다.
ko.B: 그 돌판은 하나님께서 친히 만드신 것이고, 거기에 새겨진 글씨도 하나님께서 친히 쓰신 글씨였다.
ko.R: 그 돌판은 하나님께서 만드신 것이었다. 하나님께서 그 돌에 직접 글을 새기셨다.

decisions.choice: the work of God ... the writing of God: made and written by God himself
decisions.reason: The double phrase stresses that neither the tablets nor the words came from Moses. They were written "by the finger of God" (31:18). That makes their breaking in verse 19 all the more striking.

decisions.choice: engraved: cut into the stone
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here in the Old Testament. It is related to words for carving, and means cut or incised.

source.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֧ע יְהוֹשֻׁ֛עַ אֶת־ק֥וֹל הָעָ֖ם בְּרֵעֹ֑הוַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֔ה ק֥וֹל מִלְחָמָ֖ה בַּֽמַּחֲנֶה׃

records.literal_gloss: And heard Joshua the sound of the people in its shouting, and he said to Moses, a sound of war [is] in the camp.

en.L: And Joshua heard the sound of the people in their shouting, and he said to Moses, "A sound of war [is] in the camp!"
en.B: When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, "I hear the sound of war in the camp!"
en.R: Joshua heard the people shouting. He said to Moses, "It sounds as if there is fighting in the camp!"

es.L: Y oyó Josué el ruido del pueblo en su gritería, y dijo a Moisés: «¡Ruido de guerra [hay] en el campamento!».
es.B: Cuando Josué oyó el ruido de la gente que gritaba, dijo a Moisés: «¡Se oye estruendo de guerra en el campamento!».
es.R: Josué oyó los gritos de la gente. Le dijo a Moisés: «¡Parece que hay una batalla en el campamento!».

fr.L: Et Josué entendit le bruit du peuple dans ses clameurs, et il dit à Moïse : « Un bruit de guerre [est] dans le camp ! »
fr.B: Quand Josué entendit le bruit du peuple qui poussait des cris, il dit à Moïse : « J’entends un bruit de guerre dans le camp ! »
fr.R: Josué a entendu les cris du peuple. Il a dit à Moïse : « On dirait qu’on se bat dans le camp ! »

sw.L: Naye Yoshua akasikia sauti ya watu katika kelele zao, akamwambia Musa, "Sauti ya vita [iko] kambini!"
sw.B: Yoshua aliposikia sauti ya watu wakipiga kelele, akamwambia Musa, "Nasikia sauti ya vita kambini!"
